subject: gk
question: Deba Prasad Das, Pankaj Charan Das and Gangadhar Pradhan were the famous exponents of which of the following dance forms?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Odissi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Deba Prasad Das, Pankaj Charan Das, and Gangadhar Pradhan are celebrated exponents of **Odissi**, one of the eight classical dance forms of India.
 
• Odissi originated from the state of **Odisha** and is known for its fluid movements, grace, and intricate expressions (abhinaya).
 
• Deba Prasad Das and Pankaj Charan Das contributed significantly to reviving the traditional dance form post-independence, focusing on its **ritualistic roots in temples.**
 
• Gangadhar Pradhan was instrumental in promoting Odissi globally and founded the **Orissa Dance Academy** to train future generations in this art form.
 
• Odissi performances often depict themes from Hindu mythology, especially stories of Lord **Jagannath, Krishna, and Radha**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Odissi Dance Characteristics:**

 
 
• Odissi is characterized by **tribhanga (three-bend posture)** and the **Chowka (square stance),** which form the foundation of its movements.
 
• The dance is accompanied by **Odissi music,** which is a blend of classical and folk traditions originating from Odisha.
 
• The **ghungroo** (ankle bells) worn by dancers accentuate the rhythm of foot movements.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context:**
 
 
• Odissi traces its roots back to **Natya Shastra,** an ancient Sanskrit text on performing arts written by Bharat Muni.
 
• The dance was traditionally performed by **Maharis** (temple dancers) as an offering to deities in temples, particularly Lord Jagannath's temple in Puri.
 
 
 
• **Other Classical Dance Forms of India:**
 
 
• **Bharatanatyam:** Originated in Tamil Nadu, known for its fixed upper torso and intricate footwork.
 
• **Kathak:** Originated in northern India, characterized by storytelling through expressive gestures and swift spins.
 
• **Manipuri:** Originated in Manipur, focusing on soft, graceful movements depicting themes of Lord Krishna.
 
• **Sattriya:** Originated in Assam, performed in monasteries (Satras) as a form of devotional art.
 
 
 
• **Global Recognition:**
 
 
• Odissi has gained global acclaim for its aesthetic appeal and storytelling, often performed at international cultural festivals.
 
• Efforts by institutions and dancers like Gangadhar Pradhan have contributed to its recognition as a UNESCO **Intangible Cultural Heritage.**
